Ecopetrol SA is offering dollar bonds for the first time in more than two years, the second Colombian company to tap global markets this month as it refinances debt used to fund its expansion in Brazil.
The state-owned energy company launchedBloomberg Terminal
a $2 billion bond sale, with notes due in 2034 yielding 7.98%, down from initial price talks around 8.35%, according to a person familiar with the matter who asked not to be identified. Part of the proceeds will be used to prepay a portion of a bridge loan used to acquire a stakeBloomberg Terminal
in Brazil’s Brava Energia SA.

A renewed wave of dip buying drove stocks toward their best day since April in the wake of a technology selloff that roiled Wall Street, with the market also gaining as oil prices fell.
Following a drawdown in one of the world’s most-crowded trades, a gauge of chipmakers jumped 6%. The S&P 500 rose over 2%. The Nasdaq 100 added 3%. That’s despite a 5.5% slump in Nvidia Corp. amid an investigation into Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang after his admission of an affair with a woman identified in a series of reports as a suspected Chinese spy.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Australia’s corporate regulator has opened an investigation into insolvent Sydney developer Bathla Group as its latest surveillance showed that poor practices persist in the country’s A$250 billion ($172 billion) private credit industry.
“I can confirm we have commenced a formal investigation in relation to the conduct of the affairs of the Bathla Group,” Simone Constant, commissioner for the Australian Securities and Investments Commission, said in a statement on Tuesday. “We are making inquiries in relation to private lenders but have not commenced any formal investigation at this stage,” Constant said.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Mexico’s annual inflation accelerated more than expected in October, likely to intensify scrutiny of the central bank’s decision last week to cut interest rates in the face of persistent price pressures.
Consumer prices rose 3.75% in October from a year earlier, the national statistics institute reported Monday. The reading was above all 23 estimates in a Bloomberg survey of economists, which had a 3.65% median, and up from the 3.45% reading in September.

Takeaways by Bloomberg AI
Two regional Fed Banks are aiming to look at how lending standards are evolving in the rapidly growing private credit industry through a new surveyBloomberg Terminal
announced Monday.
The survey, from the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, will “provide insights into the availability of credit, credit provision, the evolution of lending standards in private credit markets, and the implications for the broader economy and monetary policy,” according to a press release. It will also evaluate trends in loan documentation, borrower demand and the approval of new loans over the third quarter.
